Name: Planner Portal: Seating Layout & Room Intelligence
User Requirement Statement: We want a planner or a customer to open one link and step into a living shared command center for their event — not a form not an email chain not a static PDF floor plan. They see the current seating layout update in front of them as anyone else with access changes it they can see and hold the real room in their hands before committing to a plan and they never wonder whether what they are looking at is current.
Atomic Requirement: The system shall provide a real-time collaborative seating/layout editor for event planning integrated with AI-powered room intelligence access-controlled by a tiered free/paid fork model operable offline and backed by Cloudflare edge architecture — such that a planner or customer opens one link and steps into a living shared command center for their event.
Functional Requirement Specification: The Planner Portal Seating/Layout layer shall implement: (1) A public-by-default fork model for free-tier events with private-by-default access for paid-tier events URS-PLAN-001. (2) Per-event access control via signed tokens with role-based grants staff/planner/customer/guest and guest attribution URS-PLAN-002. (3) Real-time collaborative layout editing over WebSocket with last-write-wins conflict resolution per table/seat and live presence cursors URS-PLAN-003. (4) A draft/locked workflow that auto-locks events 72h before start for food-service-affecting changes with staff-only override capability URS-PLAN-004. (5) Three room-capture paths AR scan AI-guided measurement Q&A PDF/drawing upload converging on a shared capacity/clearance check URS-PLAN-005. (6) Per-event change log with undo revert and batched staff notifications URS-PLAN-006. (7) Offline-tolerant client via Cloudflare Pages + service worker with queued local edits and reconcile-on-reconnect URS-PLAN-007. (8) Tiered billing enforcement — free tier unlimited public events; paid tier flat monthly base + bundled private events + per-event overage URS-PLAN-008.
Intent / User Need: Turn proprietary technique transmission from a lecture or a manual into something the crew experience through the card game itself — so the Taza standard is absorbed in the flow of work not in a training room.
Invariants: All 8 child requirements pass their individual Acceptance Criteria. End-to-end test: a planner creates a free-tier event with a full layout (tables+guests) via the AI room-capture path invites a customer who edits a table live while the planner sees the change in real time the event auto-locks 72h before start and a staff override is logged with upcharge decision. A second user forks the public event gets a fully independent copy. The same flow works offline on reconnect. A paid-tier event is inaccessible to uninvited users. All events pass the clearance check with explicit planning estimate labeling.
Failure Behavior: End-to-end black-box test covering all 8 FRs in sequence; plus adversarial tests per child requirement (clock-skew network-loss mid-edit concurrent edits to same table stale service-worker version PDF-upload-of-menu-instead-of-floorplan billing-service-unreachable) per each child's verification method.
Acceptance Criteria: Planners and customers relying on static PDFs email chains and phone-tag to coordinate event layouts; dimension guesswork leading to seating-layout-timefield failures; no version control; no offline capability at rural venues; expensive generic tools Asana Monday that do not understand event geometry.
Verification Method: Decision-tree cost tracking referral QR codes vendor SLA monitoring and post-event feedback — these are part of the same holistic portal but specified in their own packages. The actual payment processor integration FR-8. Rectangular/banquet-table-specific clearance rules interim default used until defined.
Maintenance Requirements: 1. Does the 72-hour lock URS-PLAN-004 apply to the whole layout or only food-service-relevant fields headcount table count? 2. Pricing-model conflict URS-PLAN-008 — bundle-plus-overage vs. older V2 $50/instance flat fee. Debate team must pick one not merge both. 3. If a planner is removed from an event reassigned while a customer they invited still has active Editor access — does the customers access survive the planners removal? Needs a decision per URS-PLAN-002. 4. Rectangular/banquet table clearance rule — currently an interim default 72 edge-to-edge; needs a real rule before V1.x ships. 5. Exact monthly base price bundle size and overage fee — needs real Cloudflare usage-cost modeling once live.
External Dependencies: The seating/layout/room-intelligence layer is the centerpiece of the Planner Portal technological moat. The free-tier fork model drives organic discovery; the paid tier protects privacy. Offline capability is not optional for venues with poor connectivity. The three room-capture paths AR/AI/upload ensure no device or skill level is excluded from accurate room intelligence. Cloudflares edge architecture Durable Objects Pages Workers provides the real-time offline globally-distributed backbone without managing servers.

Name: Visibility the Fork Model
User Requirement Statement: As a planner or event host I want anyone to be able to browse and copy a public event plan as a starting point without my involvement while my paid private events stay invisible to everyone I have not explicitly shared the link with — because the free tier drives discovery and the paid tier protects privacy.
Atomic Requirement: The system shall mark every free-tier event as publicly viewable and forkable by any authenticated user showing the full plan including full guest names no redaction. A Fork action shall create a brand-new independently owned event seeded from a snapshot of the source — no shared state after that point. Paid-tier events shall be private by default: not listed not viewable not forkable by anyone the owner has not explicitly shared the link with. A forks visibility shall follow the forkers own account tier not the sources.
Inputs: Event layout state snapshot source event ID forkers account ID
Outputs: New event Durable Object with independent ownership
Trigger: User clicks Fork on a visible event
Failure Behavior: Fallback: all events private by default loses free-tier discovery but protects data. On billing/unreachable error default to blocking new fork operations rather than allowing unlimited unowned forks.
Failure Mode Addressed: An unauthorized user attempting to access a private event gets denied no partial data leak. A free-tier event is fully visible including guest names with a working Fork action to any authenticated user. Forking creates a fully independent event; editing either the original or the fork afterward never affects the other. Edge: a user forks a public event then the original owner deletes their account — the fork survives intact. A forker on a free account forks a public event which was created by a paid account while set to public — the fork is itself publicly viewable per the forkers free-tier visibility. Forking an event with a large layout 500+ seats completes within a reasonable time. Negative: paid-tier share link accidentally shared broadly — only explicitly shared-link holders can view it the event is not publicly listed. Silent failure: fork that appears complete but silently drops data e.g. missing a table or guest name — verify with post-fork audit. Guest names silently redacted on a free-tier event or conversely full names leaking on a private event — verify both states.
Out of Scope: 1) Free-tier event visibility test: authenticated user views full plan with guest names Fork button is present and functional. 2) Fork-independence test: edit source after fork verify fork unchanged; edit fork verify source unchanged. 3) Private-event denial test: unauthenticated request and unauthorized authenticated request both get denied. 4) Account-deletion fork survival test: delete source owners account verify fork remains fully functional. 5) Integrity audit: post-fork query all tables/seats/names in source vs. fork confirm byte-identical snapshot. 6) Nick will test manually.

Name: Per-Event Access Control Guest Attribution
User Requirement Statement: As a planner I need to control exactly who can see and edit each event — invite customers by email set their role and revoke their access at any time — and I need every edit attributed to a real persons first name not an anonymous cursor so I always know who changed what.
Atomic Requirement: Every access grant shall be a signed per-event token carrying event ID role staff/planner/customer/guest and level editor/viewer. A customer shall have no access at all until their planner explicitly invites them; the planner shall be able to grant change or revoke that access at any time independently per event. Any Editor-level user shall be able to invite guests; every guest shall authenticate with their own email address never a shared/anonymous identity and their first name shall appear on their cursor and in the change log for every edit.
Inputs: Event ID planners identity target users email role assignment
Outputs: Access token user can access event editor with name attribution
Trigger: Planner invites a user; user clicks shared link; user attempts an edit
Failure Behavior: Fallback: token-auth service unreachable → deny all access fail-closed. Offline: locally-cached token grants access to the last-known state with read-only capability until re-authentication succeeds.
Acceptance Criteria: Normal: new event link grants no access until planner explicitly invites; planner-granted Editor can edit live with first name on cursor/change log; guest invited by Viewer inherits only Viewer access. Edge: revoking access mid-session rejects very next write attempt; two guests with same first name — attribution unambiguous via full name on hover; planner removed while their invited customer still has Editor access — open question; guest authenticates with new email but known under old address — resolves to same identity. Negative: grant of role level unauthorized by grantors level is rejected; malformed/expired token gets clear error. Silent failure: leaked token — verify tokens are opaque and short-lived; token revocation that only takes effect on next page load but not during active WebSocket — verify revocation closes active connection within bounded time e.g. 30s.,1) Invite/deny test: uninvited user denied invited user gets correct access. 2) Edit attribution test: Editors first name appears on cursor and change log. 3) Revocation test: revoke mid-session confirm next write rejected WebSocket terminated within 30s. 4) Same-name test: two guests same first name verify hover shows full name. 5) Token-expiry test: expired token gets clear error. 6) Nick will test manually."
Maintenance Requirements: Token signing depends on Worker auth layer BUNDLE-PLANNER-CORE. Token-check on WebSocket messages inside Durable Object handler.
External Dependencies: Does a removed planners invited customers retain their access? Two approaches: a customer access is independent and survives or b customer access is transitive and dies with the planners role. Debate team decides.

Name: Real-Time Collaborative Layout Editing
User Requirement Statement: As a planner working with a customer I need to see their layout changes appear on my screen instantly as they make them and I need to know who else is in the room with me — so we are never looking at different versions and wondering which one is current.
Atomic Requirement: The system shall hold one live canonical layout tables seats room geometry per event editable over a live WebSocket connection by any connected Editor-level client with every edit broadcast to every other connected client for that event. Conflicting edits to the same object shall resolve last-write-wins scoped per table/seat never per whole layout. Every connected client shall see lightweight presence signals whos connected what theyre dragging rendered as live cursors/highlights. On reconnect a client shall request full current state rather than replaying missed edits.
Inputs: WebSocket connection user edits table/seat position cursor position
Outputs: Updated layout state broadcast to all connected clients presence signal broadcast
Trigger: Editor user modifies a table or seat; user connects to an event
Failure Behavior: Fallback: WebSocket fails → client shows last-known state with Reconnecting overlay and retries with exponential backoff. On reconnect client requests full current state.
Acceptance Criteria: Normal: two clients on same event — one moves a table the other sees it within <500ms; two clients edit different tables simultaneously both persist; same-table conflict later write wins both converge; reconnecting client receives full state. Edge: significantly wrong client clock — server timestamps used for resolution not client time; high-latency connection — server orders by receipt time not send time; 10+ simultaneous clients — presence signals remain lightweight. Negative: WebSocket drops but HTTP session valid — reconnects without data loss; mid-drag disconnect — table stays at last confirmed position. Silent failure: stale presence showing connected user as still connected — verify heartbeat timeout <2 missed; two clients both believe their edit won — verify convergence to same winner state via adversarial testing.,1) Live-edit broadcast test: one client moves table second sees it without refresh measure latency. 2) Simultaneous-edit test: two clients edit different tables then same table both converge. 3) Reconnect test: force network drop verify full state on reconnect. 4) Clock-skew test: set client clock 5 min ahead confirm server timestamp wins. 5) Presence-heartbeat test: disconnect client verify presence removed within 2 heartbeat intervals. 6) Adversarial conflict test: scripted concurrent edits to same object verify convergence. 7) Nick will test manually."
Maintenance Requirements: Depends on Durable Object per event for canonical state BUNDLE-PLANNER-CORE. WebSocket routing through Worker for token checks.

Name: Draft/Locked Workflow
User Requirement Statement: As a planner I need the event to automatically lock down food-service-relevant changes 72 hours before start so the kitchen has a firm count to prep against — no last-minute guest-count bumps without a formal override. As staff I need the ability to unlock or override with an explicit upcharge decision logged because sometimes the client does need to add two tables at T-48h and we need to track the cost.
Atomic Requirement: Every event shall default to draft editable live by any Editor-level user. The system shall automatically transition an event to locked exactly 72 hours before its scheduled start for any change affecting food service guest count table count anything feeding kitchen prep; customer and external-planner access shall become view-only at that point. Only staff shall be able to unlock or directly edit a locked event; every such change shall be flagged as an override require an explicit upcharge decision yes/no/amount before being applied and be logged with who requested it who approved it what changed and when.
Inputs: Event ID scheduled start time (server authoritative) current time
Outputs: Lock status override log entry staff notification
Trigger: Cron/scheduler ticks past lock deadline; staff performs override;
Failure Behavior: Fallback: lock job fails to fire → event flagged for manual staff review within 15 min not silently unlocked past deadline. Alert sent to staff if event passes lock deadline without locking.
Acceptance Criteria: Normal: event >72h from start editable; event at exactly 72h auto-locks; locked event rejects non-staff edits with clear message; staff override logged with full audit trail who approved what changed when upcharge decision. Edge: lock job fails to fire — event flagged within 15 min; scheduled start time changes — lock recomputes; cosmetic-only edit in locked state — open question whether override needed. Negative: customer attempting edit on locked event sees clear explanation not technical error. Silent failure: mid-edit lock transition preserves users in-flight change with lock notice and draft preserved; override logged but upcharge never followed up — revenue-leak risk verify override log surfaced in billing/invoicing review queue.,1) Auto-lock test: event at T+73h editable; advance time to T+72h verify locked. 2) Override test: staff override verify full audit log. 3) Lock-miss test: simulate job failure verify flag/alert within 15 min. 4) Time-change test: change start time verify lock recalculates. 5) Mid-edit-lock test: editing when lock fires verify graceful rejection with preserved draft. 6) Nick will test manually."
Dependency Notes: Open question: does lock apply to whole layout or only food-service fields? Whole-layout lock recommended for V1.x food-service-only as V2.x enhancement.

Name: Room Capture AI Room Intelligence Capacity Check
User Requirement Statement: As a planner or customer I need to know that my seating layout actually fits the real room — regardless of what device I am holding or whether I have a floor plan. If my phone supports AR show me. If not help me figure out the room by asking a few good questions or by reading the drawing I already have. And every layout no matter how it was created gets checked against a consistent clearance rule so tables are not too close together for food service.
Atomic Requirement: The system shall offer three ways to capture a venues real dimensions chosen automatically or by the user based on whats available all converging on the same room data object and the same capacity/clearance check: (1) AR scan device-capable capture real-world dimensions and obstacles via phones camera/AR sensors overlay planned layout on live camera at true scale. (2) AI-guided measurement fallback no AR support the systems AI asks short targeted questions gathers measurements deduces room shape from answers plus photos. (3) PDF/drawing upload planner-facing AI deduces room dimensions from the drawing reconciles against any provided measurements flagging conflict. All three paths run the same capacity/clearance check: minimum center-to-center spacing for round tables = table radius + 72 clearance; rectangular/banquet tables use 72 edge-to-edge interim. Every result labeled planning estimate never fire-code or occupancy-compliance determination.
Inputs: User device AR capability user measurement answers uploaded PDF/drawing
Outputs: Room data object capacity/clearance check result with disclaimer
Trigger: User opens room capture flow; user launches AR scan; user provides measurement answers; user uploads PDF/drawing
Failure Behavior: Fallback: manual room-dimension entry user provides length/width/obstacles directly. AI Q&A low-confidence estimate → prompt for clarification or fall back to manual entry never silently proceed with bad estimate.
Acceptance Criteria: Normal: AR-capable device offered AR path; non-AR device offered AI-guided with no AR option shown; AI Q&A produces room estimate user can override; PDF upload AI asks for reference dimension before trusting; clearance check flags tables closer than radius+72 naming both tables and shortfall; result labeled planning estimate. Edge: AI Q&A low-confidence prompts clarification or manual fallback; PDF vs. entered measurements conflict flagged for user selection; non-floorplan PDF detected and rejected; irregular room shape AR correctly captures obstacles. Negative: failed room capture path offers alternative/manual entry; empty layout clearance check shows clean no-conflicts. Silent failure: clearance math must be deterministic not AI-driven; planning estimate disclaimer must appear on every rendering surface; AR scale accuracy within 5% of real.,1) AR path test: scan known room confirm dimensions within 5%. 2) AI Q&A test: known input produces correct deduced room. 3) Low-confidence test: contradictory answers prompt for clarification. 4) PDF upload test: floor-plan PDF deduces correctly after scale calibration. 5) PDF-not-floorplan test: menu PDF rejected gracefully. 6) Conflict reconciliation test: conflicting measurements flagged. 7) Clearance check test: radius+70 fails radius+74 passes. 8) Disclaimer audit: every UI surface checked for planning-estimate label. 9) Nick will test manually."
Maintenance Requirements: AR depends on WebXR API in browser. AI Q&A and PDF call vision-capable model via AI Gateway gflip. Clearance check is deterministic function.
External Dependencies: Rectangular table clearance rule currently interim 72 edge-to-edge. Real rule accounting for rectangular geometry must be defined before V1.x ships.

Name: Change Tracking Staff Notification
User Requirement Statement: As staff I need to see every change made to an event after it was created know who made it and when and be able to undo or revert to any earlier state. I also do not want to be notified twenty times when a customer makes a burst of edits — batch it up and tell me once.
Atomic Requirement: Every applied edit shall be appended to a per-event change log tagged with the acting users identity and timestamp. The system shall support in-session undo and reverting the whole layout to any earlier logged point. Staff shall be notified batched e.g. every 15 minutes of activity or on session end not per edit whenever a customer- or external-planner-linked session edits an event in draft.
Inputs: Edit event user identity server timestamp
Outputs: Change log entry undo action revert action batched staff notification
Trigger: User applies an edit; user clicks undo; user requests revert to a logged point; customer burst of edits triggers batching timer
Failure Behavior: Fallback: no undo capability changes still tracked revert handled manually. Notification failure: fall back to queued notification delivered on next successful send.
Acceptance Criteria: Normal: every edit appended to change log with user ID and server timestamp; in-session undo reverses most recent edit; revert to earlier point restores full layout; customer edits over 15 min produce one batched notification. Edge: undo stack persists across sessions via change log; revert to locked-period point requires override if food-service fields; rapid successive reverts queued and sequential. Negative: corrupted revert target data — revert refused with error; empty change log undo shows graceful nothing-to-undo. Silent failure: change log unbounded growth — verify retention/compaction strategy; batched notification too vague — include human-readable change summary not just count.,1) Change-log test: edit appears in log with correct user/timestamp. 2) Undo test: 3 edits undo one verify state. 3) Revert test: revert to point A verify snapshot match. 4) Revert-corruption test: corrupted snapshot refused with clear error. 5) Batching test: 10 edits in 10 min produce one notification. 6) Batch-summary test: notification includes human-readable change summary. 7) Nick will test manually."
Maintenance Requirements: Change log stored in Durable Object storage for active draft. Full snapshots pushed to Postgres on lock or periodic save BUNDLE-PLANNER-CORE. Staff notifications via existing N100 path.

Name: Offline-Tolerant Client
User Requirement Statement: As a planner visiting a rural venue with one bar of signal I need the app to open instantly and let me keep working on the layout even with no internet. When I get back online my changes should sync up without losing anything or silently overwriting someone elses work.
Atomic Requirement: The app shell shall load from Cloudflare Pages edge cache and be precached by a service worker after first load so it opens instantly and remains usable with zero connectivity. Offline the user shall be able to edit solo with changes queued locally; on reconnect queued changes shall sync and the client shall reconcile to full current state under the same last-write-wins rule as URS-PLAN-003. A persistent honest UI indicator shall distinguish Live from Offline changes will sync and any conflict discovered on reconnect shall surface a visible notice never a silent overwrite.
Inputs: App shell service worker offline edit queue reconnect signal
Outputs: Sync reconciliation conflict notice Live/Offline UI indicator
Trigger: User opens app after first load; user loses connectivity while editing; user regains connectivity after offline period
Failure Behavior: Fallback: app requires connectivity degraded — offline editing lost but app shell still loads from cache for instant-on. Service worker cache invalidated while offline shows New version available reconnect to update notice.
Acceptance Criteria: Normal: app shell loads from cache with zero signal after first online load; offline edits sync and reconcile correctly on reconnect; conflicting edit from elsewhere surfaces visible notice; Live/Offline indicator matches connection state within 5s. Edge: stale service worker version — on reconnect fetch new version with update notice; edits on offline period when event gets locked — rejected on reconnect with explanation; 500+ offline edits — sync within 30s with progress indicator. Negative: first load with zero signal shows graceful offline fallback not blank page; service worker install failure does not prevent online load. Silent failure: Live indicator that reports Live when WebSocket is actually disconnected zombie connection — verify indicator reflects WebSocket heartbeat not just navigator.onLine; out-of-order sync of offline edits — verify ordered by local timestamp/sequence number.,1) Offline-load test: load once with connectivity then airplane mode verify app loads from cache. 2) Offline-edit-sync test: edits offline reconnect verify sync and convergence. 3) Conflict test: another client edits same table while offline reconnect verify visible conflict notice. 4) Indicator test: toggle connectivity verify indicator updates within 5s. 5) Large-queue test: 500 offline edits sync within 30s with progress indicator. 6) First-load-offline test: clear cache airplane mode open first time verify graceful fallback. 7) Nick will test manually."
Maintenance Requirements: Service worker via Cloudflare Pages. Offline queue in IndexedDB. Sync reconciliation uses same LWW rule as online Durable Object. WebSocket health indicator checks actual connection state.

Name: Tiered Billing Enforcement
User Requirement Statement: As the business owner I need free-tier users to be able to create unlimited public events driving discovery and viral fork growth while paid accounts pay a predictable monthly fee for private events — but proportionally more if they are a high-volume user so I am not subsidizing heavy users on a flat rate.
Atomic Requirement: Free tier public/forkable events shall be unlimited and free with no usage cap. Paid accounts shall be charged a flat monthly base fee including a bundled number of private events per month plus a small per-event overage fee beyond that bundle — enforced at the point of creating or converting an event to private with overage confirmed before it is incurred never billed as a silent surprise.
Inputs: Account tier bundle count current usage count
Outputs: Event creation approval/rejection overage confirmation prompt
Trigger: User attempts to create private event; user converts public event to private; user upgrades from free to paid
Failure Behavior: Fallback: billing/usage-count service unavailable → block creation never unlimited free overage. User shown Billing service temporarily unavailable please try again.
Out of Scope: Normal: free account creates unlimited public events; private event blocked with upgrade prompt. Paid account within bundle creates private events with no overage; paid account past bundle gets overage confirmation prompt before creation. Edge: account at bundle boundary 6th triggers overage prompt; public-to-private conversion counts against bundle; free upgrade mid-month keeps existing public events public. Negative: billing service down blocks private event creation with clear error; overage prompt dismissal defaults to no creation. Silent failure: usage counter drifting out of sync with actual event count — nightly reconciliation job alerts on discrepancy; paid account cancels mid-month — events switch to read-only at end of paid period not immediately with warning before cancellation.,1) Free-tier test: 10 public events succeed; private event blocked with upgrade prompt. 2) Bundle test: events up to bundle no overage; one past limit prompts overage confirmation. 3) Billing-unavailable test: billing service down blocks private event with error. 4) Convert-to-private test: convert public to private verify overage triggers if past bundle. 5) Counter-audit test: usage counter vs. actual event table reconciliation. 6) Nick will test manually."
Verification Method: Billing enforcement in Worker at event-creation/visibility-change time BUNDLE-PLANNER-CORE. Usage-count service must be highly available. Payment processor integration out of scope.
